pool.what: compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane
pool.rule: within 50 meV/atom of the convex hull, a band gap of at most 1 eV, magnetic or not, 2 to 5 elements, up to 40 atoms in the cell, elements Hurricane's training data covers; the list holds the 354 that Radar sends to Hurricane, one per chemical system, except the 279 too far from Hurricane's training data for it to give a chance

check.about: out of fold on the 3DSC entries: of the compounds Hurricane gave at least an even chance, the share that superconduct, against the share among the others; 139 of the 2,123 entries lie outside the training part of their fold and get no chance

novelty.about: each candidate's distance, in its model's standardized inputs, to the nearest material the model learned from; beyond the distance that separates 95% of the training materials from their nearest neighbour in another chemical system or parent compound, it lies outside the training data

caveat: Hurricane learned measured Tc from cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion compounds and other oxides; it gives the chance that a compound superconducts and its Tc if it does. Many of these compounds would need doping or pressure, and a candidate is a prediction until an experiment checks it

check.note: The authors describe the YbRhIn5 spacer as a normal metal in this thin-film stack. No standalone YbRhIn5 transition-temperature limit is assigned here. The passage does not specify an applied pressure. This observation does not exclude superconductivity in other crystal phases, doped compositions or pressure conditions, and is not a direct validation of the JARVIS structure.
check.cite: T. Asaba et al., Nat. Commun. 15, 3861 (2024)

check.note: The introduction cites prior work reporting no transition to 0.020 K. This is not a new temperature limit for every strained film. Applied pressure is unspecified in the passage; the statement does not exclude superconductivity in other phases, doping or pressure conditions.
check.cite: M. Shimozawa et al., Phys. Rev. B 86, 144526 (2012)
J. Y. Cho et al., Chem. Mater. 20, 6116 (2008)
check.note: The original paper reports a heat-capacity peak near 1.8 K attributed to magnetic order. Methods give susceptibility 2–300 K at 0.1 T and heat capacity 0.35–70 K. The heat-capacity floor must not be assigned to resistivity or treated as an explicit no-superconductivity cutoff. This audit did not establish a superconductivity absence statement to 0.35 K. Superconductivity outcome remains unknown.

check.cite: J. Y. Cho et al., Chem. Mater. 20, 6116 (2008)
check.note: The original paper reports antiferromagnetic order near 10 K. Methods give susceptibility 2–300 K at 0.1 T and heat capacity 0.35–70 K. The heat-capacity floor must not be assigned to resistivity or treated as an explicit no-superconductivity cutoff. This audit did not establish a superconductivity absence statement to 0.35 K. Superconductivity outcome remains unknown.

The publisher abstract gives a specific-heat measurement range of 0.07-10 mK (0.00007-0.01 K) for cubic Cu3Au-type PrIn3 and attributes an anomaly near 0.13 mK to nuclear magnetic ordering. This is a measured temperature range, not an established superconductivity exclusion limit. The inspected abstract does not establish absence of superconductivity; full text and the experimental conditions would be needed before assigning such a conclusion.
check.cite: Y. Karaki et al., Czech. J. Phys. 46, 2209 (1996)

reliability.about: false alarms: the share of held-out background compounds (JARVIS-DFT compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane) given at least an even chance of superconducting; an upper bound, as a few of them may superconduct
reliability.cite: T. Konno et al., Phys. Rev. B 103, 014509 (2021)
reliability.dismissed_about: called unlikely: trained without a whole family, the share of that family's superconductors given a chance under one half, averaged over the four families; a compound that gets no chance (not known) is not counted as called unlikely
reliability.unknown_about: not known: a compound further from every training compound, in the model's standardized inputs, than the given multiple of the distance that separates 95% of the training compounds from their nearest neighbour in another parent compound gets no chance

not_known.about: Hurricane gives no chance to a compound further from every training compound, in its standardized inputs, than the distance that separates 95% of the training compounds from their nearest neighbour in another parent compound; such compounds are not listed
